A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain 24 readable pages, including Appendices A–L. Text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original classifier evaluations, religious-trajectory analysis of 1,000 Holocaust testimonies, and human evaluations of trajectory similarity, with additional empirical results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the original classifier, trajectory, and human-evaluation results, including the model comparisons and supplementary analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: The segmentation procedure, RoBERTa filter, LLM valence classification, trajectory taxonomy, and DTW-based clustering remain unchanged, including the appendix prompts and clustering procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions analyze the same 1,000 English-language Holocaust testimonies for religious practice and belief. No dataset, task, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The model comparators in Table 6 and the artificial-trajectory baselines within Tables 3 and 8–10 have identical membership in both versions.

E3.justification: Preprocessing, data splits, model and prompt configurations, evaluation metrics, the 101-testimony subset experiment, and the human-evaluation selection criteria are unchanged.

E4.justification: The chronology analysis in Appendix A, filtered-versus-all-content comparison in Appendix J, density analysis in Appendix K, and clustering examples in Appendix L are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same ten-split cross-validation, seed information, inter-annotator agreement, standard deviations, and t-tests. No statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Section 7.1 changes positive belief with oscillating practice from 22% to 26%, and positive belief with active practice from 22% to 17%; both-aspects-oscillating remains 22%. These corrections match Figure 4's unchanged labels. Other numerical and qualitative results, including appendix results, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal task definition, trajectory-distance equation, and taxonomy structure and coverage definitions are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about extracting thematic trajectories, common constant-positive belief patterns, and predominantly oscillating practice patterns.

C2.justification: The discussion, limitations, and Appendix A retain the same interpretations of narrative chronology, reporting and annotation biases, applicability boundaries, and future research directions.

D1.justification: Hyperparameters, annotation guidelines, prompts, and Appendix L's clustering implementation details are unchanged. Code availability on request and archive-permission restrictions for data and models also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 2 and elsewhere are unchanged. The new acknowledgments provide contributor and funding credits rather than additional related research.

P1.justification: v4 adds an Acknowledgments section identifying institutional support, contributors, and funders, and updates the version header. The scientific prose and section sequence otherwise remain unchanged apart from the numerical corrections.

P2.justification: References and appendices reflow: Figure 7 moves from PDF page 11 to page 12, and Table 7 shifts below the Appendix H text on page 19. Figures and tables retain their content, styling, and captions.

improvement.justification: The Section 7.1 corrections resolve two discrepancies with Figure 4, improving reporting accuracy; the acknowledgments also disclose research support. The gain is limited: scientific evidence is unchanged, and Figure 4's caption still incorrectly describes the two largest joint groups as an evenly divided 44%, despite labels of 26% and 22%.
